text: Why did the OSI protocol suite fail while its model survived?
choices: The model was better designed than the protocols
It was specified before implementation, was expensive and complex, arrived after TCP/IP had the installed base, and included layers nobody needed
explanation: TCP/IP was specified by people who had already built it and came free with Berkeley Unix. The IETF's 'rough consensus and running code' is a direct statement of the difference. Layers 5 and 6 have almost no counterpart in deployed systems.
